verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो राजा पाण्डुसुतो नारदं प्रत्यभाषत । भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि सुवर्णष्ठीविसम्भवम् ॥१॥
verses.english: As in a dream this body (inactive) and the enlivening spirit in its subtile form, separating itself from the former, walks forth, so, in the state called deep sleep (or death), the subtile forin with all the senses becomes inactive, and the Understanding, separated from it, remains awake. The same is the case with Existence and Non-Existence.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु स मुनिर्धर्मराजेन नारदः । आचचक्षे यथावृत्तं सुवर्णष्ठीविनं प्रति ॥२॥
verses.english: As when a sheet of water is clear, images reflected in it can be seen by the eye, similarly, if the senses be undisturbed, the Soul is capable of being seen by the understanding.

verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथाऽयं केशवोऽब्रवीत् । कार्यस्यास्य तु यच्छेषं तत्ते वक्ष्यामि पृच्छतः ॥३॥
verses.english: If, however, the piece of water is agitated, the person standing by it can no longer sce those images. Likewise, if the senses become disturbed, the Soul can no longer be seen by the understanding.

verses.sanskrit: अहं च पर्वतश्चैव स्वस्त्रीयो मे महामुनिः । वस्तु कामावभिगतौ सञ्जयं जयतां वरम् ॥४॥
verses.english: Ignorance produces Delusion. Delusion possesses the mind. When the mind becomes impure, the five senses which have the mind for their refuge becomed corrupted also.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रावां पूजितौ तेन विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा । सर्वकामैः सुविहितौ निवसावोऽस्य वेश्मनि ॥५॥
verses.english: Overfilled with Ignorance, and sunk in their mire of worldly objects, one cannot enjoy the sweets of contentment or tranquillity. The Soul with its good and evil acts, returns again and again to the objects of the world.

verses.sanskrit: व्यतिक्रान्तासु वर्षासु समये गमनस्य च । पर्वतो मामुवाचेदं काले वचनमर्थवत् ॥६॥
verses.english: On account of sin one's thirst is never satisfied. One's thirst is then satisfied when one's sin is dissipated.

verses.sanskrit: आवामस्य नरेन्द्रस्य गृहे परमपूजितौ । उषितौ समये ब्रह्मंस्तद्विचिन्तय साम्प्रतम् ॥७॥
verses.english: On account of attachment to earthly objects, which has a tendency, to multiply itself, one wishes for things other than those for which one should wish, and accordingly fails to attain to the Supreme.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहमब्रुवं राजन्पर्वतं शुभदर्शनम् । सर्वमेतत्त्वयि विभो भागिनेयोपपद्यते ॥८॥
verses.english: From the destruction of all sinful acts, knowledge originates in When Knowledge arises a person sees his Soul in his understanding even as one sees his own image in a polished mirror. men.

verses.sanskrit: वरेण च्छन्द्यतां राजा लभतां यद्यदिच्छति । आवयोस्तपसा सिद्धिं प्राप्नोतु यदि मन्यसे ॥९॥
verses.english: One reaps misery for his senses being not controlled. One acquires happiness on account of his senses being restrained. Therefore, a person should control his mind by self-exertion from objects apprehended by the senses.

verses.sanskrit: तत आहूय राजानं सञ्जयं जयतां वरम् । पर्वतोऽनुमतो वाक्यमुवाच कुरुपुङ्गव ॥१०॥
verses.english: Above the senses is the mind; above the mind is the understanding; above the understanding is the Soul; above the Soul is the Supreme.

verses.sanskrit: प्रीतौ स्वो नृप सत्कारैर्भवदार्जवसंभृतैः । आवाभ्यामभ्यनुज्ञातो वरं नृवर चिन्तय ॥११॥
verses.english: From the Unmanifest originates the Soul; from the Soul has originated the understanding; from the understanding has' originated the mind. When the mind is united with the senses, than it apprehends sound and the other objects of the senses.

verses.sanskrit: देवानामविहिंसायां न भवेन्मानुषक्षयम् । तद्गृहाण महाराज पूजार्हो नौ मतो भवान् ॥१२॥
verses.english: He who renounces those objects as well as all those that are manifest, he who liberates himself from all things that arise from primordial matter, enjoys immortality.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । प्रीतौ भवन्तौ यदि मे कृतमेतावता मम । एष एव परो लाभो निर्वृत्तो मे महाफलः ॥१३॥
verses.english: The Sun rising spreads his rays. When he sets, he withdraws to himself those very rays that were spread by him.
verses.bhavadeepa: देवानामिति । येनं देवपीडा मनुष्यक्षयश्च न भवति तत्तादृशं वरं गृहाणेति भावः ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: तमेवंवादिनं भूयः पर्वतः प्रत्यभाषत । वृणीष्व राजन्संकल्पं यत्ते हृदि चिरं स्थितम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: Similarly, the Soul, entering the body, obtains the fivefold objects of the senses by spreading over them his rays represented by the senses. When, however, he turns back, he is said to set by withdrawing those rays to himself.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच । अभीप्सामि सुतं वीरं वीर्यवन्तं दृढव्रतम् । आयुष्मन्तं महाभागं देवराजसमद्युतिम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Continually driven along the path that is created by acts, he reaps the fruit of his acts for his having followed the practice of acts.

verses.sanskrit: पर्वत उवाच । भविष्यत्येष ते कामो न त्वायुष्मान्भविष्यति । देवराजाभिभूत्यर्थं संकल्पो ह्येष ते हृदि ॥१६॥
verses.english: Desire for the object of the senses does not affect a person who has no such desire. Desire, leaves him who has seen his soul, which, of course, is entirely free from desire.

verses.sanskrit: ख्यातः सुवर्णष्ठीवीति पुत्रस्तव भविष्यति । रक्ष्यश्च देवराजात्स देवराजसमद्युतिः ॥१७॥
verses.english: When the Understanding, shorn of the attachment to the objects of the senses, is concentrated in the mind, then does one succeed in attaining to Brahma, for it is there that the mind with with the understanding withdrawn into it can possibly be destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: तच्छुत्वा सञ्जयो वाक्यं पर्वतस्य महात्मनः । प्रसादयामास तदा नैतदेवं भवेदिति ॥१८॥
verses.english: Brahma is not an object of touch or of hearing, or of taste, or of sight, or of smell, or of any other inference. Only the Understanding can get it.

verses.sanskrit: आयुष्मान्मे भवेत्पुत्रो भवतस्तपसा मुने । न च तं पर्वत: किञ्चिदुवाचेन्द्रव्यपेक्षया ॥१९॥
तमहं नृपतिं दीनमब्रुवं पुनरेव च । स्मर्तव्योऽस्मि महाराज दर्शयिष्यामि ते सुतम् ॥२०॥
अहं ते दयितं पुत्रं प्रेतराजवशं गतम् । पुनर्दास्यामि तद्रूपं मा शुचः पृथिवीपते ॥२१॥
एवमुक्त्वा तु नृपतिं प्रयातौ स्वो यथेप्सितम् । सञ्जयश्च यथाकामं प्रविवेश स्वमन्दिरम् ॥२२॥
verses.english: Having said so to that king both of us left him for coming to where we wished, and Srinjaya returned to his palace.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जयस्याथ राजर्षेः कस्मिंश्चित्कालपर्यये । जज्ञे पुत्रो महावीर्यस्तेजसा प्रज्वलन्निव ॥२३॥
verses.english: After some time had passed, the royal sage Srinjaya had born unto him a highly powerful and energetic son.

verses.sanskrit: ववृधे स यथाकालं सरसीव महोत्पलम् । बभूव काञ्चनष्ठीवी यथार्थं नाम तस्य तत् ॥२४॥
verses.english: The child grew up like a large lotus in a lake, and became Suvarnashthivin in reality as well as in name.

verses.sanskrit: तदद्भुततमं लोके पप्रथे कुरुसत्तम । बुबुधे तच्च देवेन्द्रो वरदानं महर्षितः ॥२५॥
verses.english: This wonderful fact, O best of the Kurus, soon became widely known over the world. The king of the gods also learnt of it as the outcome of Paravata's boon.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स्वाभिभवाद्भीतो बृहस्पतिमते स्थितः ।  कुमारस्यान्तरप्रेक्षी बभूव बलवृत्रहा ॥२६॥
verses.english: Fearing humiliation the slayer of Vala and Vritra began to watch for the loopholes in that prince.

verses.sanskrit: चोदयामास तद्वज्रं दिव्यास्त्रं मूर्तिमत्स्थितम् । व्याघ्रो भूत्वा जहीमं त्वं राजपुत्रमिति प्रभो ॥२७॥
verses.english: He commanded his celestial weapon Thunder, standing before him, in embodied from saying,-Go, O powerful one, and assuming the form of a tiger kill this prince.

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृद्धः किल वीर्येण मामेषोऽभिभविष्यति । सञ्जयस्य सुतो वज्र यथैनं पर्वतोऽब्रवीत् ॥२८॥
verses.english: When grown up, this child of Srinjaya may, by his deeds humiliate me, O Thunder, as Parvata had said, thus addressed by Shakra, the celestial weapon Thunder, the subjugator of enemy's towns, began from that day to continually watch for the weak points of the prince.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु शक्रेण वज्रः परपुरञ्जयः । कुमारमन्तरप्रेक्षी नित्यमेवान्वपद्यत ॥२९॥
सञ्जयोऽपि सुतं प्राप्य देवराजसमद्युतिम् । हृष्टः सान्तःपुरो राजा वननित्यो बभूव ह ॥३०॥
verses.english: Srinjaya, meanwhile, having obtained that child who was effulgent like Indra himself, became filled with joy. The king, accompanied by his wives, and the other ladies of his household, took up his quarter in the midst of a forest.

verses.sanskrit: ततो भागीरथीतीरे कदाचिन्निर्जने वने । धात्रीद्वितीयो बालः स क्रीडार्थं पर्यधावत ॥३१॥
verses.english: One day, on the bank of the Bhagirathi, the boy accompanied by his nurse, ran here and there in play.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चवर्षकदेशीयो बालो नागेन्द्रविक्रमः । सहसोत्पतितं व्याघ्रमाससाद महाबलम् ॥३२॥
verses.english: Though only five years' old, his prowess, even then, resembled that of a powerful elephant. While thus playing the child met a powerful tiger that attacked him suddenly.

verses.sanskrit: स बालस्तेन निष्पिष्टो वेपमानो नृपात्मजः । व्यसुः पपात मेदिन्यां ततो धात्री विचुक्रुशे ॥३३॥
verses.english: The infant prince trembled greatly as he was being mangled by the tiger and soon fell down dead on the Earth. Seeing in the nurse cried aloud in grief.

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा तु राजपुत्रं स तत्रैवान्तरधीयत । शार्दूलो देवराजस्य माययाऽन्तर्हितस्तदा ॥३४॥
verses.english: Having killed the prince, the tiger through Indra's powers of delusion, vanished there and then.

verses.sanskrit: धात्र्यास्तु निनदं श्रुत्वा रुदत्याः परमार्तवत् । अभ्यधावत तं देशं स्वयमेव महीपतिः ॥३५॥
verses.english: Hearing the cries of the nurse, the king in great anxiety ran there.

verses.sanskrit: स ददर्श शयानं तं गतासु पीतशोणितम् । कुमारं विगतानन्दं निशाकरमिव च्युतम् ॥३६॥
verses.english: He saw his son there, his blood quaffed off and lying dead on the ground like the moon dropped from the sky.

verses.sanskrit: स तमुत्सङ्गमारोप्य परिपीडितमानसः । पुत्रं रुधिरसंसिक्तं पर्यदेवयदातुरः ॥३७॥
verses.english: Taking up on his lap the boy bathed in blood, and the king, with heart stricken with grief, began to lament piteously.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ता मातरस्तस्य रुदत्यः शोककर्शिताः । अभ्यधावन्त तं देशं यत्र राजा स सञ्जयः ॥३८॥
verses.english: The queen also smitten with sorrow, and crying, quickly ran where king Srinjaya was.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स राजा सस्मार मामेव गतमानसः । तदाहं चिन्तनं ज्ञात्वा गतवांस्तस्य दर्शनम् ॥३९॥
verses.english: In that plight the king thought of me with rapt attention. Knowing that the king was thinking of me I appeared before him.

verses.sanskrit: मयैतानि च वाक्यानि श्रावितः शोकलालसः । यानि ते यदुवीरेण कथितानि महीपते ॥४०॥
verses.english: Assailed with grief as the king was, I recounted to him all those stories, O king, that this hero of Yadu's race has already recited to you.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जीवितश्चापि पुनर्वासवानुमते तदा । भवितव्यं तथा तच्च न तच्छक्यमतोऽन्यथा ॥४१॥
verses.english: I restored Srinjaya's child to life with Indra's permission. That which is ordained must take place. It is impossible to make it otherwise.

verses.sanskrit: तत ऊर्ध्वं कुमारस्तु स्वर्णष्ठीवी महायशाः । चित्तं प्रसादयामास पितुर्मातुश्च वीर्यवान् ॥४२॥
verses.english: After this prince Suvarnashthivin of great renown and power began to gladden the hearts of his parents.

verses.sanskrit: कारयामास राज्यं च पितरि स्वर्गते नृप । वर्षाणां शतमेकं च सहस्रं भीमविक्रमः ॥४३॥
verses.english: Of great prowess, he ascended the throne of his father after the latter had died, and reigned for one thousand and one hundred years.

verses.sanskrit: तत ईजे महायज्ञैर्बहुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः । तर्पयामास देवांश्च पितॄश्चैव महाद्युतिः ॥४४॥
verses.english: He worshipped the gods in many great sacrifices accompanied with profuse presents. Highly effulgent he gratified the gods and the Pitris.

verses.sanskrit: उत्पाद्य च बहून्पुत्रान्कुलसन्तानकारिणः । कालेन महता राजन्कालधर्ममुपेयिवान् ॥४५॥
verses.english: Having begotten many sons all of whom by their children multiplied the race, he breathed his last, o king, after many years.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं राजेन्द्र सञ्जातं शोकमेनं निवर्तय । यथा त्वां केशवः प्राह व्यासश्च सुमहातपाः ॥४६॥
verses.english: Do you, O foremost of kings, remove this grief of your heart, as Keshava has advised you, as also Vyasa of austere penances.

verses.sanskrit: पितृपैतामहं राज्यमास्थाय धुरमुद्वह । इष्ट्वा पुण्यैर्महायज्ञैरिष्टं लोकमवाप्स्यसि ॥४७॥
verses.english: Rise up, O king, and carry the burden of this your ancestral kingdom, and celebrate high and great sacrifices so, that you may obtain (hereafter) whatever regions you may wish to acquire. Rise up, O king, and carry the burden of this your ancestral kingdom, and celebrate high and great sacrifices so, that you may obtain (hereafter) whatever regions you may wish to acquire.
